hints.content:
We can map a figure onto a **similar** figure using only rigid transformations and dilations. This means the figures must have exactly the same shapes, but may have different sizes.

For triangles in particular, two triangles are similar if all of their corresponding angles are [[☃ definition 1]].

options.definition: Angles with the same measure that we can map onto each other using rigid transformations

hints.content:
Triangle $ABC$ has angle measures of $49^\circ$ and $96^\circ$. The third angle measure is therefore $180^\circ - 49^\circ - 96^\circ = 35^\circ$.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: Triangle A B C. Angle A is ninety-six degrees. Angle B is forty-nine degrees. Angle C is thirty-five degrees

hints.content:
Triangle $QRS$ has angle measures of $49^\circ$ and $96^\circ$. The third angle measure is $180^\circ - 49^\circ - 96^\circ = 35^\circ$.



[[☃ image 1]]

Therefore $\triangle QRS$ is similar to $\triangle ABC$.

options.alt: Triangle Q R S. Angle Q is ninety-six degrees. Angle R is forty-nine degrees. Angle S is thirty-five degrees

hints.content:
Triangle $XYZ$ has angle measures of $41^\circ$ and $38^\circ$. The third angle measure is $180^\circ - 41^\circ - 38^\circ = 101^\circ$.



[[☃ image 1]]

Therefore $\triangle XYZ$ is not similar to $\triangle ABC$.

options.alt: Triangle X Y Z. Angle X is one hundred one degrees. Angle Y is forty-nine degrees. Angle Z is thirty-eight degrees

hints.content: In conclusion, only $\triangle QRS$ is similar to $\triangle ABC$.
